title.zh: 有限直角束网格射线交点

summary: Replay the FIDASIM finite rectilinear grid_intersect branch: enumerate the six box faces in the source's +x,-x,+y,-y,+z,-z order, pair the first valid face with the first later distinct valid face, and order entry/exit along the ray.

identity.relation: For side s in (+x,-x,+y,-y,+z,-z): a candidate face point exists only when the direction component on the face axis is nonzero and the other two coordinates of the point stay inside the closed side bounds; the first valid face and the first later valid face more than 0.001 cm away form the unique pair; dot(direction, delta) orders entry and exit along the ray direction. No pair means length 0, both points backfilled with the input origin and intersects_grid=False. This discrete face order is part of the contract, not a generic slab test. The enumeration is an infinite-line face-pair test with no origin-side check: the ordered pair may lie entirely behind the ray origin (e.g. an origin outside the slab with the direction pointing away still reports intersects_grid=True), and an origin inside the grid legitimately reports its entry behind the origin. The 'entry' output is ordered relative to the pair, not guaranteed forward of the origin; callers needing forward-only geometry must validate the returned points themselves.
identity.direction: ray origin/direction + grid center/full lengths -> entry point, exit point, chord length, intersection flag
identity.definition: The saved FIDASIM grid_intersect finite rectilinear branch (src/fidasim.f90:8685-8814), consumed by the mc_nbi initial grid entry and reusable for any caller-owned finite-grid ray handoff. The operator does not judge in_plasma; that remains a framework-side decision.
identity.model: the saved formal implementation, ported verbatim with registered finite-length and finite-output gates
identity.geometry: one finite axis-aligned rectilinear box; source-ordered face enumeration
identity.coordinates: positions in cm; ray direction/velocity scale does not affect the ordered pair
identity.boundary: finite shape-[3] origin/direction/center; grid lengths finite and strictly positive (registered: NaN lengths rejected); tangential degeneracy or missing distinct pair yields the origin-backfilled zero-length result
assumptions: The caller supplies a finite rectilinear grid state and a continuous ray.
The in_plasma decision on the entry point is owned by the consuming framework edge, not this operator.

inputs.name: ray_direction
inputs.description: Ray direction or velocity; scale does not affect the ordered pair.

inputs.name: grid_lengths_cm
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive (registered: NaN lengths rejected).

outputs.name: entry_point_cm
outputs.description: First valid face intersection in the dot(direction, delta) pair ordering; backfilled with the input origin when no distinct pair exists. Not guaranteed forward of the ray origin (the source performs no origin-side check; see identity.relation).
outputs.constraints: Finite; may lie behind the ray origin for origins inside the grid or pairs behind the origin.

outputs.name: exit_point_cm
outputs.description: Second distinct valid face intersection; backfilled with the input origin when no distinct pair exists.

outputs.name: intersection_length_cm
outputs.description: Euclidean chord length between the two intersections.
outputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; zero when no distinct pair exists.

outputs.name: intersects_grid
outputs.description: Whether two distinct valid face intersections exist.

preconditions: A finite axis-aligned rectilinear grid state and a continuous finite ray.
supported: Single-ray finite-grid entry/exit handoff for NBI birth trajectories, lines of sight or particle tracks.
excluded: Field interpolation inside the grid, trajectory advancement, in_plasma masking and native runtime equivalence.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when any ray or grid vector is non-finite or misshaped, or when a grid length is non-positive or non-finite (registered hardening; the saved arm's positivity test lets NaN lengths through to a silent no-intersection result).
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if the selected intersection geometry is non-finite for finite but extreme input magnitudes (registered hardening).
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; the no-intersection result is the source-defined complete answer.

example.description: The saved package's forward probe: a ray entering through -x and leaving +x returns the source-ordered pair.
example.code:
from scirel.fusion import intersect_ray_with_rectilinear_grid
result = intersect_ray_with_rectilinear_grid(
    ray_origin_cm=[-2, 0, 0], ray_direction=[1, 0, 0],
    grid_center_cm=[0, 0, 0], grid_lengths_cm=[2, 4, 6])
assert result['intersects_grid'] and result['intersection_length_cm'] == 2.0
assert list(result['entry_point_cm']) == [-1.0, 0.0, 0.0]
assert list(result['exit_point_cm']) == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]
try:
    intersect_ray_with_rectilinear_grid(
        ray_origin_cm=[0, 0, 0], ray_direction=[1, 0, 0],
        grid_center_cm=[0, 0, 0], grid_lengths_cm=[2, float('nan'), 2])
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('NaN grid lengths must be rejected (registered hardening)')
example.expected: The forward probe reproduces the saved ordering and chord; NaN grid lengths raise ValueError.

scope: Saved-package probe reproduction (forward/reverse ordering, miss and degenerate zero-length returns).
Saved infinite-line pair semantics pinned as a contract: no origin-side check, pair may lie behind the origin.
Registered hardenings: finite grid lengths and finite intersection geometry.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The maintained direct tests reproduce the saved package's own probes (forward and reverse face ordering, tangential and missing-second-face degeneracies) and exercise the fail-closed contracts including the finite-length gate. The face enumeration is closed-form geometry; no grid-internal interpolation, in_plasma masking or whole-trajectory composition is asserted. The saved FIDASIM packages ship package-level oracles rather than a pinned source-runtime replay target, and the recorded implementation digest provides the provenance linkage. No test establishes the relation against an external physics reference beyond the source closed form.
known_limitations: No forward-only guarantee: intersects_grid and the ordered pair follow the source's infinite-line face enumeration, so a ray pointing away from the grid can still report a pair behind the origin; forward-only callers must validate the returned geometry.
